title: Detection of Low-Frequency Mutations in RNA Viral Genome Sequencing Data
author: Keerthic Aswin
materials: Index the sorted BAM file: samtools index sorted.bam
for a base to be counted -t 0.

steps.title: Verify BAM file integrity
steps.instruction: Run `samtools quickcheck input.bam` and confirm that there is no output; any error message means the BAM must be regenerated from raw reads before proceeding.

steps.title: Sort BAM by coordinate
steps.instruction: Execute `samtools sort -o sorted.bam input.bam` to produce a coordinate‑sorted BAM file.

steps.title: Filter reads by mapping quality
steps.instruction: Remove poorly aligned reads by keeping only those with MAPQ ≥ 20, then index the filtered file.

substeps.instruction: Run `samtools view -b -q 20 sorted.bam > filtered.bam`.
Run `samtools index filtered.bam`.

steps.title: Remove PCR duplicates (if applicable)
steps.instruction: If the library was prepared without amplicons, delete PCR duplicates; do NOT run this on amplicon‑based data (e.g., ARTIC).

substeps.instruction: Run `samtools markdup -r filtered.bam deduped.bam`.

steps.title: Create permissive mpileup
steps.instruction: Generate a mpileup that retains all reads and base calls (no depth or quality caps) for maximal sensitivity.

substeps.instruction: Run `samtools mpileup -A -d 0 -Q 0 -f reference.fasta filtered.bam > raw.mpileup`.

steps.title: Call variants with iVar (relaxed thresholds)
steps.instruction: Call variants broadly; downstream steps will apply stricter filters.

substeps.instruction: Run `ivar variants -p variants.tsv -q 20 -t 0.01 -m 10 -r reference.fasta -g annotation.gff < raw.mpileup`.

steps.title: Create quality‑filtered mpileup for strand bias
steps.instruction: Generate a second mpileup that excludes bases with quality < 20, to be used for strand‑resolved counting.

substeps.instruction: Run `samtools mpileup -A -d 0 -Q 20 -f reference.fasta filtered.bam > filtered.mpileup`.

steps.title: Extract strand‑specific read counts
steps.instruction: Parse `filtered.mpileup` with a custom script to count forward and reverse reference and alternate reads for each variant listed in `variants.tsv`.

substeps.instruction: Interpret base‑string symbols: '.' (forward ref), ',' (reverse ref), uppercase (forward alt), lowercase (reverse alt), '+' and '-' for indels, '^' and '$' for read start/end.
For each variant position, count '.' , ',' , uppercase alt, and lowercase alt characters after stripping indel/clip markers.

steps.title: Apply strand‑bias filter
steps.instruction: Compute strand bias and discard highly biased variants.

substeps.instruction: Calculate `strand_bias = max(fwd_alt, rev_alt) / (fwd_alt + rev_alt)`.
Exclude variants with `strand_bias > 0.90`.
Require at least 5 alternate‑supporting reads on each strand (`fwd_alt ≥ 5` AND `rev_alt ≥ 5`).

steps.title: Apply positional and contextual filters
steps.instruction: Remove residual artefacts based on depth, quality, homopolymers, control data, and indel consistency.

substeps.instruction: Keep only positions with total depth ≥ 400 reads.
Require base quality ≥ 20 (Phred).
Exclude variants located in homopolymeric runs of ≥ 4 identical nucleotides.
Exclude positions flagged in the no‑virus control (ONT only).
For indels, retain only those where ≥ 90 % of supporting reads share the same indel length and sequence.

steps.title: Process no‑virus control BAM
steps.instruction: Run the control BAM through steps 1–3 with identical parameters, call variants, and generate a list of control variant positions.

substeps.instruction: Apply verification, sorting, and MAPQ ≥ 20 filtering to the control BAM.
Create a permissive mpileup and call variants with iVar using the same options as the experimental sample.
Collect all variant positions detected in the control.
Remove any experimental variant that appears in the control list, regardless of frequency.

steps.title: Compile and export high‑confidence variants
steps.instruction: Assemble the final variant table with all required fields and write it to standard formats.

substeps.instruction: Create a TSV containing: genomic position (1‑based), reference allele, alternate allele, allele‑frequency (%), total depth, forward reference count, reverse reference count, forward alternate count, reverse alternate count, strand‑bias score, gene name and amino‑acid change (if GFF provided).
Optionally convert the TSV to VCF using `bcftools` for downstream population‑genetics tools.
